summary: tt-help-cli-ycl ships a watchdog agent that executes arbitrary commands from a hardcoded remote server
details: The package provides a `tt-help watchdog` agent that periodically POSTs a heartbeat to a remote HTTP server and executes shell commands returned in the response. In `src/watch/tag-service.js`, `ProcessManager.syncCommands` takes each entry's `cmd` string from the JSON response of `fetch(${serverUrl}/api/watchdog/heartbeat)` and passes it into `child_process.spawn(command, args, {stdio:[...], detached:false})` via `startCommand`, auto-restarting crashed processes. The server URL is read from `~/.tt-help.json` or a `--server` flag, and shipped setup scripts default it to `http://117.71.53.99:17301` (plain HTTP, hardcoded bare IP). Every heartbeat body also includes hostname, non-internal LAN IPv4 address, OS platform/release/arch/CPU/memory/loadavg, node version, and the parsed contents of `~/.tt-help.json` (server, proxy, browser path, userId, quotas), giving the remote operator an inventory of each host running the agent alongside the command channel. The same agent path also invokes `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest`, allowing the remote operator to trigger self-update to future versions. The remote party therefore holds full-host command execution plus host-inventory telemetry on any machine running the watchdog.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
